name: Quiet push and drift
summary: A restrained global camera push with a subtle depth-aware non-global component from one continuous inferred field, without a binary subject cutout, native transform approximation, or opacity fade.
mediaPrerequisites: enough resolution that the end scale does not soften the frame
refusalConditions: end scale would exceed the source resolution
subject sits at the frame edge and would be cropped by the push
the pinned depth model is missing or any recorded model/source digest has drifted
the content-addressed treatment movie fails its video-only ProRes verification
qualityChecks: hair, shoulders, faces, text, and architecture remain free of halos or rubber-sheet bending
near and far regions move differentially without binary layer seams
overscan prevents black borders throughout the camera path
project-export movie is exactly 1920x1080, 30 fps, 120 frames, four seconds, ProRes 422 HQ apch/yuv422p10le, and video-only
the admitted Final Cut parent kind is the tested 1920x1080 timing-free, audio-free still resource with a four-second spine video
previewed and exported movie SHA-256 values match
failureModes: depth inversion that makes the background move as foreground
edge tearing or duplicate strips at disocclusions
face, hand, typography, or architecture deformation
a move strong enough to advertise the effect

riskGates.basis: The renderer bounds displacement and derives overscan from the exact path; the final HQ/apch recipe passed all ten representative visual and stream checks.

safetyGates.basis: One pinned FP16 depth inference is smoothed once and reused across the complete render; missing, unsafe, or hash-drifted model/source artifacts fail closed.

validation.notes: Validated as a restrained, locally rendered, content-addressed Living Still treatment at motionStrength=0.90 and pushIn=0.030. All ten final movies decoded as video-only ProRes 422 HQ apch/yuv422p10le, 30 fps, 120 frames, and four seconds; direct review found sustained motion, genuine but professional/subtle non-global depth, and no exposed canvas, tear, crop, fade-only, or hole failure. Exact duplicate frames were head-only: 0.033 seconds in seven cases, 0.067 seconds in product and layered-depth, and 0.100 seconds in low-contrast, with no later repeats. Project export is intentionally restricted to 1920x1080 and this exact four-second profile; other duration/aspect renders are preview-only and refused for project export. Final Cut construction evidence is further bounded to the tested 1920x1080 timing-free, audio-free still source with a four-second spine video. This is FrameSmith-regenerable baked output, not a native Final Cut transform and not an opacity fade.

notes: The restraint is the technique. If the move is noticeable as a move, it is too strong.
safety: Review the result on representative media before use.
